title: Lab 2C — SQS decoupling
topic: SQS standard vs FIFO, DLQ, visibility timeout, long polling, EventBridge → SQS, producer/consumer decoupling
format: 15 timed scenario questions (~24 min, ~96 sec each). Reinforces night-13-sqs-decoupling.md and night-13-lab-sqs-setup scripts. Answer without peeking at night-13-quiz-answers.json first.
answerDistribution: A×4 B×4 C×4 D×3 — options shuffled so correct letter varies

questions.question: Global Ski Atlas runs Iceland as a monthly Fargate batch job (Night 12). A separate stats-uploader worker should process completions without polling ecs:DescribeTasks in a loop. What integration service best buffers completion events between the batch job and the uploader?

options.A: Amazon SNS — fan-out push to email and Lambda when the batch job completes
options.B: AWS Step Functions Express — sync workflow invoked from the Iceland container on exit
options.C: Amazon SQS — producer sends or EventBridge routes; consumer polls at its own pace
options.D: Amazon API Gateway REST with VPC Link and ECS integration for completion callbacks

questions.question: A Lambda consumer processes SQS messages that take up to 3 minutes. The queue visibility timeout is 30 seconds. What problem will you see in production?

options.A: Messages are permanently deleted from the queue after 30 seconds regardless of outcome
options.B: The same message becomes visible again while Lambda still runs — duplicate processing
options.C: SQS extends visibility automatically for all Lambdas without event source mapping setup
options.D: FIFO ordering breaks because visibility timeout must be at least 60 seconds on standard

questions.question: The Iceland completion queue receives one message per successful monthly run. Order between months does not matter; maximum throughput is desired. Which queue type should you create?

options.A: SQS standard queue — at-least-once delivery, best-effort ordering, highest throughput
options.B: SQS FIFO queue without content-based deduplication — strict order for monthly runs
options.C: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ — managed broker with durable queues and dead-letter exchanges
options.D: DynamoDB stream with Lambda event source mapping — stream records trigger the uploader

questions.question: night-13-lab-sqs-setup.sh sets maxReceiveCount to 3 on the main queue with a redrive policy pointing at saa-study-gsa-iceland-completion-dlq. What does this accomplish?

options.A: Silently deletes poison messages from the main queue after three receives without configuring any DLQ
options.B: Automatically retries failed EventBridge rule invocations and resends every event to the main queue
options.C: Guarantees exactly-once delivery of every message that reaches the DLQ after three tries
options.D: Moves messages to the DLQ after three failed processing attempts (received but not deleted)

questions.question: An EventBridge rule targets an SQS queue with FailedInvocations in CloudWatch. The rule event pattern is correct. What is the most common fix on the queue side?

options.A: Enable SSE-SQS encryption on the queue and attach a customer-managed KMS key policy for EventBridge
options.B: Attach the AmazonSQSFullAccess managed policy to the default event bus resource policy for the account
options.C: Queue policy allowing events.amazonaws.com sqs:SendMessage with aws:SourceArn = rule ARN
options.D: Rename the queue with a .fifo suffix and enable content-based deduplication for targets

questions.question: A stats-uploader worker polls an empty completion queue thousands of times per hour, increasing cost and API throttling risk. Which ReceiveMessage parameter reduces empty responses?

options.A: DelaySeconds set to 900 on SendMessage — delays new message visibility for 15 minutes
options.B: WaitTimeSeconds long polling (up to 20) — SQS holds the request until a message arrives
options.C: MessageGroupId on a standard queue — groups empty polls into one long-poll batch per group
options.D: CloudWatch alarm on ApproximateNumberOfMessages — suppresses ReceiveMessage when empty

questions.question: You need a single worker pool to absorb spikes from many producers without push delivery to every worker. SNS already fans out to five Lambdas. What should sit in front of one consolidated worker tier?

options.A: SQS standard queue — workers pull messages; the buffer absorbs producer bursts safely
options.B: A second SNS topic subscribed to the first — chains fan-out so five Lambdas forward to one
options.C: EventBridge custom event bus with no targets — buffers events until a rule is attached later
options.D: AWS AppSync GraphQL subscription — WebSocket push from producers to one consolidated pool

questions.question: A malformed JSON message causes the consumer to throw on every attempt. The operator wants to inspect failures without blocking the main queue forever. Which configuration pair is required?

options.A: Message retention of 60 seconds on the main queue only — poison messages expire quickly
options.B: SNS topic subscribed to the main queue with email — failure notifications to operators
options.C: Visibility timeout set to 0 — messages return to the queue immediately on every receive
options.D: DLQ plus RedrivePolicy maxReceiveCount on the source queue for poison-message isolation

questions.question: A payment ledger requires strict ordering per customer account and no duplicate debits. Throughput is moderate. Which SQS option fits?

options.A: Standard queue with a random MessageDeduplicationId on each SendMessage call
options.B: Standard queue with DelaySeconds 300 — staggers debits five minutes apart per customer
options.C: FIFO queue with MessageGroupId per customer and content-based deduplication enabled
options.D: EventBridge schedule expression rate(1 second) — serializes ledger writes via timed triggers

questions.question: A consumer receives a message, crashes before calling DeleteMessage, and visibility timeout is 60 seconds. What happens to the message?

options.A: The message is permanently removed — unacknowledged receives count as fully processed
options.B: After visibility timeout it becomes visible again for another consumer — at-least-once
options.C: SQS immediately moves the message to a DLQ even when no redrive policy is configured
options.D: EventBridge detects the consumer crash and republishes a duplicate ECS Task State Change

questions.question: Night 12 EventBridge schedule triggers Iceland RunTask. Night 13 adds an ECS Task State Change rule → SQS. How does that split responsibilities?

options.A: Night 12 answers when to run; Night 13 decouples post-success work from the batch container
options.B: Night 13 replaces the Night 12 schedule rule — only one EventBridge rule may exist per event bus
options.C: SQS becomes the scheduler and calls ecs:RunTask directly instead of relying on the EventBridge cron
options.D: Night 13 removes the need for iam:PassRole on the ECS execution and task roles for RunTask

questions.question: An exam question shows producers in us-east-1 and a consumer in eu-west-1 that must share a work queue with minimal latency to the consumer. What is the best answer?

options.A: Single SQS queue in us-east-1 — cross-Region ReceiveMessage is free with negligible latency
options.B: FIFO queue with a global endpoint — AWS routes polls to the nearest Region automatically
options.C: EventBridge default bus in us-east-1 — replicates all events automatically to every Region
options.D: SQS queue near the consumer (or replicate events) — SQS is Regional; cross-Region adds cost

questions.question: After sending ten messages you call GetQueueAttributes for ApproximateNumberOfMessages and see 7, then 10 a few seconds later without new sends. Why?

options.A: SQS lost three messages due to the approximate counter rounding down under high send volume
options.B: The DLQ redrive policy absorbed three messages automatically without any consumer receives
options.C: The attribute is approximate — eventually consistent; not a real-time exact count for exams
options.D: Visibility timeout expired on three in-flight messages and SQS deleted them from the queue

questions.question: night-13-lab-sqs-setup uses an event pattern on ECS Task State Change with containers.exitCode [0] and taskDefinitionArn prefix for globalskiatlas-backend-k8s-iceland. A task exits 1 after S3 upload fails. What happens?

options.A: The failed message is sent directly to the DLQ because exit code 1 matches the redrive policy filter
options.B: No completion message is enqueued — pattern requires exit 0; add a failure path (Night 14 SNS)
options.C: EventBridge retries ecs:RunTask automatically until the container exits successfully with code 0
options.D: SQS receives the ECS event anyway with exitCode 1 because the rule matches all STOPPED tasks

questions.question: Night 14 will add SNS so one Iceland failure alert reaches email and a Lambda simultaneously. Why is SNS a better fit than a single SQS queue for that requirement?

options.A: SNS fan-out push delivers one publish to many subscribers without shared-queue polling
options.B: SQS cannot integrate with Lambda — only SNS supports Lambda as an event notification target
options.C: SNS guarantees strict FIFO ordering across all email and Lambda subscribers for the topic
options.D: SQS standard queues natively support email protocol — one queue delivers to inbox and Lambda
